newsitem.title: USA: NTSB's Hall wants more cargo safety.
newsitem.headline: NTSB's Hall wants more cargo safety.

text.p: Collision avoidance equipment on cargo aircraft is a top safety priority for the National Transportation Safety Board, the chairman told Reuters on Monday.
"Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) is the most wanted item we have regarding cargo aircraft," James Hall, chairman of the National Transportation Safety Board said Monday.
TCAS is the primary type of aircraft collision avoidance equipment. It is currently required on commercial passenger aircraft in the United States, but not on cargo aircraft.
"We'd like to see the major cargo carriers voluntarily make this decision," Hall said. "But now it really looks like it is going to take Congress to step in and take action."

The National Transportation Safety Board was created 30 years ago to investigate transportation accidents and promote safety. It has no regulatory or enforcement powers, but Hall said about 80 percent of its recommendations become law or regulation.

"The size of the cargo fleet is now becoming substantial," he said. The Air Freight Association estimates there are about 900 cargo aircraft in the United States without collision avoidance equipment.
The Airline Pilots Association has asked Congress and the Federal Aviation Administration to require the installation of such equipment by 1998.
The cargo industry, especially integrators such as Federal Express and United Parcel Service, support a different technology for collision avoidance. That system, however, is still under development.
Hall also said he would like to see better training and human resource practices for cargo workers.
"We have more and more outsourcing and more and more turnover in personnel. These people have to be equipped with the same level of expertise and training," he said.
"The human factor accounts for about 80 percent of all accidents," Hall said.
